project.name: The Forest
project.objective: Build a persistent, measurable, recursively optimized autonomous production system that advances through canonical state and executable continuation.

evidence: cross-repository CI fetch attempts 34696938814 and 34696955428 exposed missing repository/network transport authority

warrant.objective: Complete live structural-authority registry integration without creating a shadow source of truth by supplying the verified read-only adapter through an authorized transport or mount.
warrant.selection_reason: The read-only registry adapter, explicit UNAVAILABLE behavior, environment boundary, and canonical-address integration test are implemented and passing in normal CI. The remaining proof gap is transport: the current GitHub Actions token cannot read the separate structural-authority repository and the runner has no general network access. The next leverage point is an authorized registry transport/mount that feeds the same replaceable adapter rather than embedding a second registry.
procedures: obtain canonical registry through an authorized read transport
mount or inject registry without copying canonical authority
resolve known Forest addresses through the runtime adapter
tests: actual canonical IDs resolve through runtime adapter
runtime cannot mutate canonical registry through resolver

quality.completion_claim_policy: No completion without ledger evidence and explicit verification. Completion of one phase must not be conflated with completion of Forest as a whole.
quality.known_verification_gap: A read-only live-registry adapter is implemented, failure behavior is explicit, and the expanded runtime suite passes CI. The actual structural registry was independently inspected through the connected GitHub capability, but an executed cross-repository runtime resolution remains unverified because the CI token cannot read the separate structural-authority repository and the execution container has no network route to GitHub. The adapter criterion therefore remains in progress rather than passed.

permissions.external_execution: must be explicitly configured by runtime operator/environment
permissions.cross_repository_ci_read: not currently available from the implementation repository workflow token; live registry transport must be mounted or supplied by an authorized connector/runtime

decisions.decision: Keep executor injection replaceable rather than hard-code a single agent/provider into the kernel.
Retries require an explicit recovery policy and are bounded by max_retries.
Regenerate the next production warrant from canonical task state after each persisted continuation pass rather than hand-maintaining duplicate control state.
Prefer compact continuation observations plus deterministic gap derivation over duplicating dashboard state as a second source of truth.
Validate canonical state before execution and again after telemetry and warrant regeneration but before persistence; invalid durable state must not silently advance.
Passing the runtime verification ledger closes the runtime-kernel phase only; the production ledger must extend into the next Forest growth phase rather than returning global DONE.

Use the whole-product stack as a responsibility/composition lens mapped onto existing canonical homes, not as a new authoritative hierarchy. Keep ThreadMap and deeper cellular/mycelial hypotheses experimental until separately validated.
Give each persistent thing one logical Forest identity across all stores and representations; derive resolver indexes from canonical registries rather than maintaining a shadow identity database.
Compress the seven exposed cross-layer interfaces into a shared family of address, resolution, mutation, and observation envelopes while preserving authority and verification boundaries.

When the runtime cannot directly read the structural-authority repository, solve the boundary with an authorized transport or mount into the replaceable registry adapter. Do not commit a copied forest.json as runtime truth merely to make integration tests pass.

history.summary: Established repository-resident canonical runtime state after persistence, bounded recovery, and CLI control surface were implemented.
Implemented a portable subprocess executor with bounded observable failure results and automatic production-warrant regeneration; advanced the ledger from 5/10 to 7/10 criteria implemented.
Implemented reconstructable continuation telemetry and deterministic gap scanning, integrated observation before persistence, and advanced the ledger to 8/10 criteria implemented.

Implemented JSON Schema enforcement at runtime boundaries, added validation regression tests, and advanced the implementation ledger to 9/10 while preserving end-to-end execution as an explicit verification gate.
First repository-native CI run failed because pytest was not installed; failure preserved as evidence rather than counted as verification.
Declared test dependencies, repaired traceback-unsafe validation exceptions, aligned runner fixtures with canonical schema, and achieved 25/25 passing runtime tests in GitHub Actions.
Closed the verified runtime-kernel phase and opened whole-product architecture reconciliation using a provisional sketchpad map rather than falsely declaring Forest complete.

Reconciled all 11 provisional whole-product responsibilities against existing canonical architecture, removed five duplicate-home risks, promoted ten supported composition relationships into a canonical whole-product map, preserved experimental boundaries, and opened a seven-contract cross-layer integration phase.

Defined one logical Forest address/resolution contract in the canonical structural repository, compressed seven cross-layer interfaces into shared mutation/observation envelopes, implemented a replaceable runtime address parser/resolver with explicit provisional and ambiguity behavior, and verified the expanded runtime suite in GitHub Actions. Opened live canonical-registry adapter integration as the next bounded unit.

Implemented a read-only canonical-registry adapter and live-integration test surface, then attempted two direct cross-repository CI transports. Both attempts failed before runtime tests because the workflow environment lacked a usable route/authority to the separate structural repository. The failure was isolated to transport rather than hidden by copying the registry.

Made live registry availability an explicit capability boundary, restored credential-independent CI, and verified the expanded runtime suite successfully in GitHub Actions job 103562050852. The live-registry criterion remains in progress until an authorized transport/mount executes the cross-repository resolution test.
